title: MothLight annotated harvest + quick wins
body:
Quick orientation (what this is):
- Scratchpad for MothLight: my lightweight synthesis of several papers + an experiment plan. Not a polished summary — written for immediate experiments and handoff.
- Goal: capture intuition and a 2-week playbook to test whether prefix distillation + episodic chunking reduces token cost while preserving QA accuracy on long dialogs.

Papers / posts I skimmed (fast takeaways):
1) "Sparse Episodic Prefixes" (arXiv 2027) — idea: store small prefix vectors per episode, match by dense embedding, prepend matched prefixes to current prompt.
   - Strength: cheap memory footprint, fast retrieval.
   - Risk: prefix drift over long sessions -> mismatch.
   - Implementation note: embedding index must support near-real-time writes. Consider HNSW with batched commits.

2) "Chunked Compression for Long Contexts" (ICLR 2028 talk) — hierarchical compression: chunk -> summarize -> index. Emphasis on staged loss: preserve QA-relevant spans.
   - Strength: predictable reduction in tokens and end-to-end SLO control.
   - Risk: summarizer hallucination; needs selective fidelity.
   - Implementation note: reuse our Optimize pipeline to score chunk importance (token-level attention heuristics).

3) "Prefix Distillation via Teacher Sampling" (blog post) — train small prefix generator by querying a large teacher on sampled episodes and store distilled prepended tokens.
   - Strength: learns to encode context signals compactly.
   - Risk: teacher cost for distillation; brittle if domain shifts.

My synthesis: "MothLight" = lightweight episodic prefix distillation + chunked selective compression.
- At write time: split session into variable-length chunks (boundary heuristic: speaker change + punctuation density + topic shift score).
- For each chunk: produce two artifacts: 1) small distilled prefix (32-128 tokens) generated by a tiny teacher distiller, and 2) a compressed summary (50–200 tokens) when chunk importance is high.
- At read time: retrieve k nearest prefixes (by chunk-level embedding) + top-n compressed summaries (by recency + importance), prepend prefixes first, then include compressed summaries only if SLO permits.

Why this might win vs naive caching:
- Prefixes are directly in-model consumable content (work well immediately for decoding).
- Summaries provide fallback when prefixes miss details.
- Two-tier retrieval lets us trade latency/cost by toggling whether we include summaries.

Open questions (priority):
- How to train the prefix distiller cheaply? Can we use a two-step distillation: offline teacher distill batches during low-cost hours -> incremental online student updates?
- Eviction strategy for prefixes: use TTL + access frequency + topical novelty.
- Risk of compounding errors: prefixes might bias the student model to stale behavior. Need evaluation probes.

Experiment plan (2-week sprint):
Week 1 (setup + baseline):
- Dataset: internal long-dialog QA corpus (customer support transcripts). Create 500 episodes of ~5–20k tokens.
- Baseline: current KV-cache + sliding-window summarization (what we already have). Measure: end-to-end latency, token cost per response, top-1 answer accuracy on held-out QA set.
- Prototype prefix distiller: use small Llama-13B-ish teacher to generate candidate prefixes from episodes. Student = 1B distiller finetuned via MLE on teacher outputs (quick fine-tune).
- Build simple HNSW index for prefix embeddings (OpenAI-style embedding or our in-house).

Week 2 (ablation + scale):
- Ablation A: prefixes only vs summaries only vs prefixes+summaries.
- Ablation B: varying prefix lengths (32, 64, 128). Track accuracy vs token cost.
- Safety checks: run hallucination probe set (specially constructed anchor facts) to verify prefixes don't introduce false claims.
- Measure: cost per 1k queries simulated at various concurrency (1–100 qps) to estimate infra scaling.

Immediate quick wins / hacks to try now:
- Use existing small summarizer (optimize pipeline) to make cheap summaries for high-attention chunks; route as fallback.
- Implement a cheap offline distillation loop: sample 1k episodes, teacher->student, test prefix retrieval recall. If recall > 0.6 for QA hits, move to online.
- Add a lightweight prefix filter: discard prefixes with low teacher perplexity delta (i.e., teacher didn't gain much by adding prefix).

Evaluation metrics (practical):
- Primary: QA F1 on held-out set; Delta vs baseline >= -2% tolerated if cost savings > 25%.
- Secondary: token-per-response, p99 latency, prefix recall@k for ground-truth supporting chunk.
- Safety: hallucination rate on anchor facts, false-positives introduced by prefix text (binary).

Notes on infra:
- HNSW memory: estimate ~0.6GB per million prefixes at 768 dims. We expect < 1M prefixes in POC. Good.
- Need a fast merge path for online writes to avoid blocking inference lanes. Add write buffer + async flush.

Questions to discuss with Mira/Devin:
- Operational limits: can Dedicated customers opt into prefix storage in their VPC? Data residency implications.
- Can we expose a policy to clients: max_prefixes_per_user, ttl, encryption at rest?

To-do (short):
- [ ] Create 500-episode evaluation pack (Keisha) — due Mon 6/19.
- [ ] Minimal distillation script + readme (Devin) — due Wed 6/21.
- [ ] HNSW prototype + insert/lookup demo (Mira) — due Fri 6/23.
- [ ] Safety probe generation (Noah) — due Fri 6/23.

Loose thread ideas (for later):
- Combine with routing policies: store prefixes in cheaper storage and route retrieval to cheaper region for non-SLA-critical requests.
- Learn an importance scorer jointly with distillation.
- Explore compressive transformer style recategorization (but lighter-weight).

Random notes / friction points I kept seeing in papers:
- Many papers assume stable distribution; production chat has huge drift. We need re-distillation triggers.
- Human-in-the-loop verification for compressed summaries reduces hallucination but adds cost. Maybe use synthetic checks (anchor facts).

Endnotes / links I want to keep handy:
- ICLR talk recording link (watch next): https://iclr.org/2028/video/chunked-compression
- Prior internal PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/optimize/pull/213 (chunk scoring heuristics)

If anything else: quick sync Tuesday 10am with Mira/Devin/Noah — add agenda items: distillation budget, evaluation pack specs, infra write path.
